question.text: Portfolio return 14%, risk-free 6%, beta 0.8. Treynor ratio (approx):

explanation.text: The Logic: Treynor ratio = (portfolio return - risk-free rate) / beta = (14% - 6%) / 0.8 = 8% / 0.8 = 10%, i.e., 0.10. The Trap: The other values come from arithmetic slips in the excess return or in dividing by beta. Note: Treynor uses beta (systematic risk) in the denominator, unlike Sharpe which uses total risk (standard deviation).
